solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Overwhelmed by drink, sailors make mistakes

indicators.note: something overwhelmed by another is engulfed by it, so the sailors sit inside the drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink, a sip or mouthful
a ship's crew are its sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors who have had too much to drink start getting things wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To screw up is a slang phrasal verb for blundering, the same as making errors.

clue.text: Son put off

parts.note: to lay something is to put it down

explanation.surface: A son has been put off doing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put off' reads as one phrase, but 'off' alone is the definition, the slang verb to kill.
explanation.definitionFit: To off someone is slang for murdering them, to kill.

clue.text: Smooth guy, comparatively little

parts.note: to guy someone is to mock or tease them, to rib them
less is the comparative of little

explanation.surface: A suave man who is rather small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' looks like a man but is the verb to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface with no raised ridges is even and flat, without ribbing.

clue.text: African court introducing large fine

indicators.note: introducing a letter brings it inside, so the large abbreviation goes into the word for court

parts.note: to woo is to court someone romantically
L is the abbreviation for large in clothing sizes
F is the abbreviation for fine on pencil grades

explanation.surface: An African court hands down a hefty fine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wolof are a people of Senegal and Gambia in West Africa, and one of them is an African.

clue.text: Doctor no doubt under pressure struggling to grow

indicators.note: in a down clue the rearranged letters sit under the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor who is undoubtedly stressed and having a hard time.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot-bound plant has roots filling its pot, which stunts its growth until repotted.

clue.text: Bibulous, hence shut up on dry island

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another is placed after it, so the hush comes last

parts.note: hence, meaning therefore, gives so
TT, teetotal, is the crossword shorthand for dry or abstaining
sh is the interjection telling someone to be quiet

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker is told to keep quiet while stuck on an alcohol-free island.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone given to drinking too much; sottish comes from sot, a drunkard.

clue.text: Waterlogged earth beneath turf

indicators.note: in a down clue the earth goes beneath the turf

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf
an earth is a fox's den

explanation.surface: Soggy soil lying below the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodden ground is soaked through with water.

clue.text: Attempt to suppress every sign of uncertainty and disloyalty

indicators.note: to suppress something is to hold it down inside, so the word for attempt encloses the rest

parts.note: a try is an attempt
each is every one
er is the hesitant sound of someone unsure

explanation.surface: A bid to stamp out any sign of doubt and betrayal.
explanation.definitionFit: Treachery is betrayal of trust, the act of being disloyal.

clue.text: Deeply thoughtful, cool present?

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool
the present is a grammatical tense, an example flagged by the question mark

explanation.surface: Someone thoughtful and chilled who is in the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: An intense person is earnest and serious, given to deep feeling and thought.

clue.text: Gratefully received by George and Kenneth alternately

parts.note: by George is an exclamation of surprise, like heavens

indicators.note: alternately takes every other letter of the name Kenneth

explanation.surface: Something gratefully received by two men called George and Kenneth in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George and Kenneth' look like two people, but 'by George' is the exclamation; 'alternately' takes ENT from KENNETH.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heaven-sent arrives as if a gift from above, so it is welcomed with gratitude.

clue.text: Wandered about, suffering a tumble in trailer?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit within the short word for a trailer

parts.note: a film trailer is an advertisement, an ad

indicators.note: words that are suffering are knocked about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who fell over while wandering around a caravan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trailer' suggests a caravan to tumble about in; the question mark flags its film sense, an advertisement. 'suffering' is the anagram signal on A TUMBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ambulate is a formal verb for walking, so having ambulated is having walked or moved about.

clue.text: Painting reversed on back of The Times supplement

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another follows it, so the turned painting comes last
the back of a word is its final letter, here of the word The

parts.note: the times sign in multiplication is an X

indicators.note: reversed tells us to write the word for painting backwards

parts.note: painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: An art section printed back to front in a newspaper's supplement.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is something additional, a supplement added to the usual.

clue.text: Leading characters in English Faculty glow, leaving university and flourishing

indicators.note: leading characters are the first letters of the words English and Faculty
the university abbreviation leaves, so it is taken out of the word for glow

parts.note: fluorescence is a glow given off by a substance under radiation

explanation.surface: A university's English faculty is thriving now that it has broken away.
explanation.definitionFit: Efflorescence is a noun for blossoming, the bursting into flower or full development of something.

clue.text: Lost my final set, without question

indicators.note: lost suggests things gone astray, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tennis player laments losing the deciding set.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifestly means plainly or obviously, beyond any doubt.

clue.text: Response lacking weight: inept, pointless and silly

indicators.note: lacking means the weight abbreviation is dropped from the word for response

parts.note: an answer is a response

indicators.note: pointless means the abbreviation for point is removed from the word inept

explanation.surface: Criticism of a weak, clumsy and pointless reply.
explanation.walkthrough: INEPT without PT, the abbreviation for point, leaves INE.
explanation.definitionFit: Anserine literally means goose-like, and since geese are proverbially foolish it also means stupid.

clue.text: Sketch bum when undressed

parts.note: a rough is a preliminary sketch or draft

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means bad or faulty, so these letters are put wrongly

explanation.surface: An artist sketches a naked backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undressed' looks like naked, but it is the stonemason's sense: dressed stone is smoothed, so undressed stone is left rough.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone or timber that is only roughly shaped, not dressed or finished, is crudely cut.

clue.text: Almost undo part of jacket?

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of its full length

parts.note: to reverse a decision or action is to undo it

explanation.surface: Someone nearly unpicking a section of their jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Revers are the turned-back lapels of a jacket or coat, showing the lining.

clue.text: Reprehensible boyfriend keeping naked girl up until exhausted

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the boyfriend letters enclose the turned girl
in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom
naked means stripped of its outer letters

parts.note: a girl is a female

indicators.note: exhausted means emptied, leaving only the outer letters of the word until

explanation.surface: A disgraceful man keeps a naked girl awake until she is worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naked girl' is a stripped synonym, not a name: 'naked' removes the outer letters of the word for girl, and 'up' reads what is left upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Blameful means deserving blame, culpable or worthy of censure.

clue.text: Cruise briefly reorganised to pick up American drowning victim

indicators.note: picking up a passenger takes them in, so the rearranged letters hold the American
reorganised tells us the shortened letters are put in a new order
briefly means the word is cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: A cruise is rearranged to collect an American passenger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts CRUISE to CRUIS, 'reorganised' makes ICRUS, and A goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the youth flew too near the sun, his wax wings melted and he drowned in the sea.

clue.text: Airman advanced over Roman road to river

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the first piece above the rest

parts.note: via is Latin for road, as in the Via Appia

explanation.surface: An airman passing above a Roman road on the way to a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator is a pilot, someone who flies aircraft.

clue.text: Diana excluding outsiders after bad year, like Shakespeare's Olivia

indicators.note: after means the trimmed name comes behind the other pieces

parts.note: ill can mean bad, as in ill effects

indicators.note: excluding outsiders keeps only the inner letters of the name Diana

explanation.surface: Diana, after a bad year, has dropped her outsider friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivia is a countess in Twelfth Night, which is set in Illyria, so she is a native of that land.

clue.text: Local detective following padre, regularly showing guts

indicators.note: following means the detective comes after the letters from padre

parts.note: a local is a pub, an inn

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of padre

parts.note: DS is a detective sergeant

explanation.surface: A local police detective tails a priest who displays courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes AR from PADRE. 'guts' looks like courage but means entrails.
explanation.definitionFit: Innards are the internal organs, the entrails or guts.

clue.text: Disparages batsmen's performances

definitions.meaning: to run down or criticise someone, to belittle them
in cricket an innings by a batsman is informally called a knock

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: a batsman's innings is called a knock.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both criticises and, in cricket slang, innings played by batsmen.

clue.text: Hospital probes shock treatment, warning about secondary symptom

indicators.note: something that probes pushes inside, so the hospital letter goes into the injector

parts.note: an EpiPen is an adrenaline injector used to treat anaphylactic shock
an omen is a warning sign
on can mean about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A hospital investigates electric shock therapy amid warnings over its side effects.
explanation.definitionFit: An epiphenomenon is a secondary effect that accompanies a condition without causing it.

clue.text: Explosive piece of reporting retracted

indicators.note: retracted means drawn back, so the letters are read in reverse
piece of means a run of letters is taken from inside the word reporting

explanation.surface: A bombshell report is withdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitro is short for nitroglycerine, a powerful explosive.

clue.text: Green flag, beach's second

parts.note: to flag is to droop or tire, to sag

indicators.note: second picks the second letter of the word beach

explanation.surface: A green flag flying over a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage is a greyish-green colour named after the herb.

clue.text: Half-heartedly shred book

indicators.note: half-heartedly means losing half of the doubled middle, one of its two central letters

parts.note: a tittle is a tiny amount, a shred or jot

explanation.surface: Someone tearing up a book without much enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Publishers call each book they issue a title, as in a list of new titles.

clue.text: A holiday atmosphere returning after opening of Chinese restaurant

indicators.note: after means the other pieces follow that opening letter
the opening of a word is its first letter, here of Chinese

parts.note: a fete is a festival or feast day, a holiday

indicators.note: returning means the word for atmosphere is written backwards

parts.note: an air is an atmosphere or mood

explanation.surface: A festive mood comes back once the new Chinese restaurant opens.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafeteria is a self-service eatery, a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: Support for privates in Axis war zones

parts.note: the y-axis is one of the two axes of a graph
fronts are the zones where armies fight

explanation.surface: Soldiers in the Axis forces at the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axis' looks like the WWII alliance; it is the y-axis. Y-fronts are British men's briefs with an inverted-Y seam.
explanation.definitionFit: These briefs support a man's genitals, his private parts, punning on army privates.

clue.text: King on throne to visit butcher's?

indicators.note: in an across clue the king set on the throne comes after it

parts.note: throne is slang for the toilet, the loo
K is the abbreviation for king in chess
to see someone, a doctor say, is to visit them

explanation.surface: The king on his throne is going to visit the butcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butcher's' is cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook means look, so a butcher's is a quick glance.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for a quick look at something.
